newsitem.title: USA: TransTexas sees Lodgepole production rise.
newsitem.headline: TransTexas sees Lodgepole production rise.

text.p: TransTexas Gas Corp said the third successful well in its new North Dakota oil field was expected to raise daily gross production from the field to 6,000 barrels of oil per day.

Flow tests of this most recent well, the Dinsdale 1-3, flowed at a rate of 5,105 barrels of sweet, 41 degree gravity crude and 1.6 million cubic feet of natural gas per day, with a flowing tubing pressure of 350 pounds per square inch.
TransTexas owns a 71.2 percent working interest in the Dinsdale 1-3.

Since the current production allowable for each of the wells in the field is 2,000 barrels daily, completion of the Dinsdale 1-3 is expected to increase gross daily production from the field to 6,000 barrels per day, it explained.

TransTexas said its current company-wide net crude oil, condensate and liquids production has increased 220 percent from the level of a year ago, to over 17,900 barrels per day, largely as a result of the initial wells in this Lodgepole field. Production from the field is realizing premium pricing per barrel as compared with West Texas Intermediate as a result of the high quality of oil located in the reservoir, it said.

TransTexas said it is drilling another, separate 3-D seismic anomaly in the City of Dickinson with its City 1-2 well, which is now at about 8,000 feet. The company has permitted three further locations in this indicated reef that it believes could contain analogous reserves.
TransTexas said it is also participating in two adjacent wells, operated by third parties, that may further extend the productive area of the carbonate reef play.
The Kostelecky 33-1 located almost one mile to the north, is operated by DuPont Co's Conoco and is being completed for Lodgepole reef production.
The Heart River 1-9 well, which is located one half mile to the south, is being drilled by Duncan Energy Inc.
